meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 5: Building Servers
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: A stdio server runs fine from its project directory but fails when launched by the desktop host with args ['run', 'server.py']. What is the most likely fix?

options.text: Add a port to the config so the host can reach the server over localhost
Use an absolute path: the host launches the process from a different working directory
Switch the server to the HTTP+SSE transport, which the host launches with its own defaults
Add Mcp-Session-Id to the config so the host can resume the connection

questions.explanation: Relative paths assume a working directory the host does not share. stdio has no port; HTTP+SSE has been deprecated since 2025-03-26; sessions were removed in 2026-07-28.

questions.question: You want non-technical users to install a local filesystem server with one click and no toolchain. Which packaging fits?

options.text: Remote Streamable HTTP, so there is nothing for the user to install at all
A Docker image, published to the registry with an OCI ownership label
MCPB: the stdio server and its runtime bundled into one installable archive
An npm package the user runs with npx, which requires only Node

questions.explanation: MCPB bundles a local server together with its runtime for one-click install without a development environment. A remote HTTP server needs no install but cannot touch the user's filesystem; npx and Docker both require a toolchain.

questions.question: Which pair of measures does the tools spec ask implementations to provide around tool execution?

options.text: Rate-limit the model's calls, and require re-authentication every 15 minutes
Sign every tool definition, and verify the signature before each call
Log all calls to a remote SIEM, and block tools without annotations
Show the user which tools are exposed, and confirm before sensitive operations

questions.explanation: The spec asks for UI that makes clear which tools are exposed, visual indicators when tools are invoked, and confirmation prompts so a human stays in the loop. Clients should also show tool inputs before the call, to catch exfiltration attempts.

questions.question: Your server exposes get_data, get_data2 and get_data_v3, each with a one-word description. The model keeps picking the wrong one. What is the fix the specification points at?

options.text: Add a readOnlyHint annotation to each one so the model can tell them apart
Reorder tools/list so the most common tool is returned first
Give each tool a distinct name and a description saying when to use it
Merge them into one tool and pass a mode string as an argument

questions.explanation: Tool selection is driven by the name, description and inputSchema the model sees, so those are the surface to fix. Ordering should be deterministic for prompt caching but does not steer selection, and annotations are untrusted hints rather than selection aids.

questions.question: Your filesystem server takes a path argument and reads it. A call arrives with ../../../../etc/shadow. What is the server's obligation?

options.text: Validate the argument itself and refuse anything outside its configured root
Ask the authorization server whether this user holds a files:read scope for that path
Return the file, since path checking belongs to the client that built the argument
Return the file, since the host already obtained the user's approval to call the tool

questions.explanation: Arguments arrive from the model and are untrusted no matter how well authenticated the connection is, so a server validates its own inputs against its own boundary. Host approval covers whether to call the tool, not whether the argument is safe.

questions.question: One of your tools takes about four minutes and the user sees nothing until it finishes. What does the protocol give you, and what does it depend on?

options.text: notifications/progress, sent on any long request whether or not a token was supplied
notifications/progress, sent only when the request's _meta carried a progressToken
notifications/message at the info level, which every client is required to display
A partial result returned early, followed by a second result when the work completes

questions.explanation: Progress is opt-in: the client puts a progressToken in the request's _meta and the server sends notifications/progress carrying that token. With no token there is nothing to correlate, so no progress is sent, and results are never returned twice.

questions.question: Your server enables an extra tool once the user links their billing account, but connected clients keep showing the old list. What should the server do?

options.text: Return -32601 for calls to the old list until each client reconnects
Shorten ttlMs on tools/list so clients discover the change when the cache expires
Include the new tool in the next tools/call result so the client learns about it
Send notifications/tools/list_changed so clients re-fetch tools/list

questions.explanation: list_changed notifications exist precisely for this and take precedence over any TTL a client is holding: on receipt the client invalidates its cached list and re-fetches. Waiting for a TTL to lapse is slower and errors teach the client nothing.

questions.question: You run three replicas of a server behind a round-robin load balancer. A tool needs two rounds of user input. What makes this work without sticky routing?

options.text: The load balancer pins the client to one replica for the lifetime of the tool call
The server encodes its context into requestState, which any replica can verify and continue
The client repeats every earlier answer on each retry, so the server needs to keep nothing at all
The replicas share a session store keyed by the JSON-RPC id of the first request

questions.explanation: That is the point of MRTR: the server puts what it needs into requestState, protected for integrity, and the client echoes it back. Any stateless instance can then reconstitute the context, which is why no sticky routing or shared session store is needed.

questions.question: A tool marks a parameter of type number with x-mcp-header. What must a conforming Streamable HTTP client do?

options.text: Exclude that one tool from tools/list and log a warning
Send the header anyway, rounding the value to the nearest integer
Ignore the annotation and call the tool normally
Reject the entire tools/list response as invalid

questions.explanation: x-mcp-header may only annotate primitive parameters: string, integer or boolean, with number explicitly excluded. A violating tool definition is invalid, and the client MUST exclude just that tool so one bad definition does not break the rest.
